items.author: Ben (2026-09-25, the round-feedback form after the sprint-47 live clicks); filed by Claude
items.title: Roads are a tree plus a detour test, and only villages above a size spur: no lattice, and round 6's tail inside 35 s
items.design:
MOVED (2026-10-07, the sprint 49 close-out; Ben: place by subject): sprint 49 -> 50. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-25, the density form): the village spur floor is 40,000 heads (the ladder's ~p90; median road pass 18 s loaded, 1 of 16 seeds under 10 s), size read as the population step's headcount; a border link ends ONLY on a town or a spurring village (LOGISTICS.md § 4). The street carpet is not this item's: BL-1130 (centres consolidate) thins the centres upstream, and this item's "no lattice on the densest seed" is read after it.

ROUND 2 (the lane's own findings and the settle review): fix the floor at 40,000 as the constant; border endpoints restricted to towns and spurring villages; road_generation.cpp's two hand-written cache clears (~616-619, ~689-691) replaced by invalidate_logistics_caches so the new nearest-anchor field is never missed; the loading bar's roads weight (hard_coded_world.cpp ~495, 38,000 ms) and kBorderUnitsPerNation re-measured; road_generation_harness's "R2 highway tier reachable when qualified" FAILS on 0 of 8 seeds, identically on b03fd52e -- find why (the percentile gate, the two-major-endpoints rule, or the harness's qualified regen) and fix the cause or split it to its own item with the reading; never weaken the row.

SPRINT 48 CUT (Ben, 2026-09-25, the cut form): BL-1077 (village roads cost) is FOLDED IN. Its target joins this done-when: generate_roads under ~10 s Release on the library seeds, read after the spur floor; if the floor alone does not reach it, BL-1077's bound (one multi-source search per centre, or a shared reach field, digest-neutral by itself) is this item's second step. THE 35 s IS JUDGED ON THE WHOLE TAIL, jointly with BL-1117 (settle tick one), which joins the sprint with its fix: on seed 0 the settle is ~56 s Release, tick 1 alone 38.5 s, so roads alone cannot meet it.

FILED 2026-09-25 (Ben, walking round 6: "we also need many fewer roads... it should be heavily discouraged to build a lattice of roads"; he chose the tree plus a detour test over "no second path", and spurs only for villages above a size). LOGISTICS.md § 4 carries the rule; STARTUP.md § Round 6 carries the 35 s target.

THE WORK. (1) Replace the relative-neighbour redundancy edges with the DETOUR TEST: after the Kruskal MST, a candidate link between two centres is laid only when the network's route between them costs more than 2x the direct A* route (one constant, named). The percentile rationing of loops applies to the loops the test admits (a delegated reading that keeps BL-618/BL-621 intact; Ben may overturn). (2) A village lays a spur only above a size floor, MEASURED on the 16 curated seeds first (Rule 0b: road tiles, spur count and pass time per floor candidate). (3) The border link rule is unchanged.

A WORLD-MOVER: every road digest and the sweep pins move -- read road tile counts, pass time (gen_step_costs --finish) and the haulage baseline (memory: goldens cannot see trade) on the 16 seeds before and after, then ONE re-bless.

DONE WHEN. No lattice on a capture of the densest seed; road pass time and tile count recorded old -> new per seed; round 6's tail lands within 35 s of arrival on seeds 0 and 28 in Release (gen_step_costs); one re-bless; road_generation_harness green (connectivity held). CARRIED to sprint 49 at the sprint 48 close (2026-10-04): owed R4 a quiet Release gen_step_costs run on 16 seeds (road tiles and pass time per seed, old -> new, against ~10 s); R6 an isolated haulage reading of this change (or fold into BL-1165); R7 a cold review of round 4 (8b921ee6, directed paths).

items.author: Claude (BL-1172 cold review, 2026-10-03)
items.title: The construction panels predict the build rate the tick will actually take
items.design: MOVED (2026-10-07, the sprint 49 close-out; Ben: place by subject): sprint 49 -> 51. construction_panel.cpp:60 and selection_panel.cpp:267 predict a site's rate from m->supply[r]. The tick draws from shelf inventory gated by the fair-price ceiling (shelf_admits, components.hpp), pauses a build on a material posted over the ceiling, and stretches it on capacity over the ceiling (FINANCE.md, Ben 2026-10-03). Needs a live click to verify.

items.author: Claude (the BL-1186 routing lane, 2026-10-04)
items.title: A convoy is drawn, seen and interdicted along the legs it actually travels
items.design:
MOVED (2026-10-07, the sprint 49 close-out; Ben: place by subject): sprint 49 -> 50. PULLED INTO SPRINT 49 (2026-10-04, the BL-1186 cold review): not only drawing - position, vision and interdiction read the unconfined centre-to-centre path, so a land-fallback convoy is interdicted on water it never enters and immune on the land it crosses, a capture credits the pool of a water tile, and a hostile unit on a sea route's inland leg never intercepts. items.author: Claude (the sprint 49 close-out; Ben, the close-out form, 2026-10-07)
items.title: A built processor gets its inputs: 85% running and at most 5% input-starved at handoff
items.design: TARGETS RAISED (Ben, 2026-10-08): G1 >= 85% running at handoff, plus G1b <= 5% input-starved (now, or decommissioned after starving), 16 seeds. 70% had no recorded reason beyond a first stretch from a 17.6% baseline; G1 alone counts a plant idled for want of a buyer as failure, so starvation gets its own target. CARRIED from sprint 49 (Ben, the close-out form, 2026-10-07: close with G1 unmet, carry it to sprint 50 as a logistics item). The 16-seed market_viability reading on main after BL-1183 C1: G1 54.7% of built processors running at handoff against Ben's 70% (G2 54.4 and G3 88.9 pass). About a quarter of built processors are already decommissioned by the handoff, and by their last reported state almost all were input-starved (half A: 578 of 674). Diagnose which inputs fail to arrive, at which markets, and why - no producer within reach, a producer whose surplus is not dispatched, or a dispatch the margin refuses - then fix the cause in the network or dispatch, not by clamping the loss reflex. Re-measure construction stalls here too: whether a stalled site is ever abandoned (BL-1183 C3) is still unruled. Judge it on the market-viability skill, 16 seeds.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-07, the supply lever form: levers 1-3, sprint 50 widens, G1 70% stays); filed by Claude
items.title: Mines that sit under construction or decommissioned are found out and fixed at the cause
items.design: MERGED (778c9f3d, 2026-10-08; five review rounds; save v38): stack-rank estimate; forecast and dead-market vetoes; a bid = demand + silenced want + off-book want (held for the cadence) + launch fuel + own-pool upkeep + running consumers; chain-start grant. Spacecraft-components plants in play 0 -> 22 on 5 seeds; idle mines 1588 -> ~180. Small follow-up in flight (bl1227-followup). SELL DIAGNOSIS (2c6e8734, 2026-10-08): of 257 mine closures in play beside a market posting >= 1.5x, 150 best markets trade nothing and 179 are unreachable; 222 had no room at any reachable candidate; revenue at the most dispatch could place 3.69/t vs cost 3.95/t - the closures are mostly correct; the reflex misjudges 17 (7%). So more mines (the ranking round ee4c10ca) is not the G1 lever. PATH (Ben, 2026-10-07): f5cbcde7 merged; the ranking round ee4c10ca is merged only after the fibre/hides boom it sets off is diagnosed and fixed (G1 path B: more mines on fresh ground). From the BL-1217 inflow diagnosis (inflow_probe round 2, d04faa9c/f9b3e9e7, 5 seeds, consumes on, cold-checked): processors want ~2-4x the raw silica / copper ore / rare earth ore their bodies produce (49% / 63% / 28% system-wide); not staffing (contention 1.0, targets ~180%), not over-building processors (0.6-0.8 per mine). Site-reads per probe: silica 393 under construction and 77 decommissioned against 630 live; copper ore 280 / 320 against 536; rare earth 302 / 255 against 315. Restarting them (with the other levers) would close 23-69% of the deficit. DIAGNOSE FIRST: why each sits - construction stalled on a material (BL-1183, the ceiling stall; abandonment C3 still unruled), never funded, or decommissioned by the loss reflex (and why the mine lost money). Then fix the cause, not by clamping the reflex (Ben rejects forced outcomes).

From the BL-1217 inflow diagnosis (inflow_probe round 2, d04faa9c/f9b3e9e7, 5 seeds, consumes on, cold-checked): processors want ~2-4x the raw silica / copper ore / rare earth ore their bodies produce (49% / 63% / 28% system-wide); not staffing (contention 1.0, targets ~180%), not over-building processors (0.6-0.8 per mine). Steel is NOT short (production / want 101% once want is corrected for other binding inputs) but its starved users are refused: ordered 31% (dispatch_convoys skips a (corp, body, good) under a standing sell order), gate 25%, noroom 28% (upper bound). items.author: Claude (the BL-1228 mine upkeep diagnosis, 2026-10-07)
items.title: A building buys power from any generator its roads reach, not only from its own market
items.design: MERGED (88391b7f, 2026-10-07; three cold-review rounds): wired provinces join a grid by roads and straits; power drawn across markets at the buyer market price; grid-level shelf cap; power-only (capacity unchanged). 5 seeds: mines at the floor 40.7% -> 21%, scalar 0.77 -> 0.87; G1 flat. Generation-less grids: BL-1232. SETTLED DESIGN, PARTLY BUILT: LOGISTICS.md § 3a (Ben, 2026-08-31) - power rides the road network; connectivity not distance (tile_reach_cost as a boolean); one tick flat latency; a buyer clears against any generator its roads reach, so power has a regional price. BL-708 (power as a grid, closed complete) built the listing gate (a market sells power only when on the grid, market_clearing.cpp ~1404-1455) but NOTHING moves power between markets: the building upkeep draw reads only its own market's shelf and pool. FOUND by mine_upkeep_probe (88984ec4, 5 seeds, replay agrees with the real step on 32,538 of 32,538 building-ticks): 95% of extraction sites' supply-scalar loss is power, 94.6% of it "none at its market while another market or pool on the body holds power"; 72% of silica / copper / REE mines are unmet every tick and pinned at the 500 floor; mean scalar ~0.72. Restoring the scalar closes ~24% / 54% / 11% of the BL-1217 deficit. WORK: let a connected market's power clear against generation on any market its roads reach (one tick), as § 3a says; measure on the market-viability skill, 5 seeds, before/after.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-07, the sprint 50 path form); filed by Claude
items.title: Every wired power grid has generation on it, so roading a province does not strand its buildings

items.author: Ben (2026-10-07, the sprint 50 path form); filed by Claude
items.title: Generation places processors in proportion to the input supply they can reach
items.design: MERGED (6cf81da2, 2026-10-08; three cold-review rounds): spare-supply test at t_idle in every pass; spare counted once and bounded per consumer; a refused processor's in-reach want enters derived demand as a shortage of its own; roster to a fixed point. 5 seeds: G1 59.3 -> 73.9, G1b 29.8 -> 20.0, G2 58.8 -> 64.2; generation-built starved 364 -> ~70; the remaining gap is the settle scorer on seed 0 (BL-1234). Ben (2026-10-07, the path form, G1 path C; extends BL-1185, chain-feasible placement). inflow_probe (cold-checked): bodies produce 28-63% of the raw silica / copper ore / rare earth ore their processors want, system-wide; processors per producer 0.6-0.8, but each mine yields a co-extraction basket so its share of any one good is small. BL-1185 made a chain feasible (a site exists); this item makes it SIZED: a processor is placed only where the input supply it can reach (by the market-viability reach rules) covers a run. DIAGNOSE FIRST: per body and good, processors placed vs the extraction that can feed them at handoff, and which generation pass places the surplus processors; then propose the rule (no clamp, a placement consequence).

items.title: A building the dial means to restore is not decommissioned by the loss reflex while the dial's hold runs
items.design: RULED (Ben, 2026-10-08, the dial lever form): the loss reflex never counts a dial-idled plant's maintenance as a loss streak, and the dial's hold on a zeroed plant ends when its own forecast recovers (AI_OPPONENT.md, the candidate table). items.author: Claude (sprint 50, deferred by Ben 2026-10-09)
items.title: Long-term viability: plants running at handoff are still running at play tick 50
items.design: DEFERRED from sprint 50 (Ben, 2026-10-09: 'push the long term viability work for another sprint, after the various other gameplay loops are settled'). Target carried: G1 at tick 50 >= 85% (market-viability; reported, not gated, in sprint 50). FOUND (starve_trace_probe, f98d43df, shipped code before sprint 50's wave 2b): of 665 plants lost handoff->t50, 386 starved. (1) STEEL: a background-firm CONSTRUCTION BOOM - on 33 starving markets 725 sites draw steel at t50, 701 background-owned (ports/hubs 264, food 181, fuel 79); site need ~373/tick vs processors ~35; making builds read steel scarcity is a NEW AI GRANT (raise it). (2) UNDELIVERED HAULS: copper ore - dispatcher 'would send' in 36/47 cases, arrivals ~8/tick; split Logistic Points cap / one-destination-per-pass / goods sent elsewhere (SUPPLY/LOGISTICS). (3) POOL-HELD STOCK: 42 plants starve while stock sits unlisted in other pools at the market; split processor reservation vs sell-order floor (MARKETS). (4) FUEL->PROPELLANT COLD START: with generation bounded by want, neither chain stands at generation and no launchpad exists on any seed; space access depends on settle/play building both (PRODUCTION, ERAS gate). Ruled healthy, keep: fair-price ceiling (cf off: -8.0 G1t50), background pull (cf off: -1.4), households' first draw. Re-measure with the probe after sprint 50 merges before designing.

items.author: Claude (sprint 50 PROPELLANT cold review; backlogged by Ben 2026-10-09)
items.title: A rival's launch fuel is not drained by its own scorer or the space programme - or it is, by ruling
items.design: BACKLOGGED by Ben (2026-10-09, launch fuel form) - both questions open, for a ruling when space access matters. Context: MARKETS.md step 4 reserves a pad pool's propellant from auto-surplus (Ben 2026-10-09; may still be sold by a standing order). Cold review of the PROPELLANT lane found three rival paths that ignore that reservation: (a) corp_ai.cpp listable_surplus (~2572) uses processor_reservation, so the trade candidate places an uncapped sell order that empties the pad pool, re-placed each time stock rebuilds; (b) the scorer's directed dispatch (~2735) has no reservation and can haul pad propellant to the capital market on the same body; (c) space_programme.cpp (~140-175) buys 50-unit lumps from the pool holding most unreserved stock - pad pools are now where propellant piles up. Q1: should the scorer sell/haul only above the pad reservation? Q2: should the space programme buy only the excess? No seed had a launchpad at t50 in sprint 50, so the effect is latent.

items.author: Claude (sprint 50, BL-1119 R7 review + stale-flood measurement; Ben 2026-10-09)
items.title: Road generation lays no long parallel road beside a serviceable one, at near the stale-flood pass time
items.design: RULED (Ben, 2026-10-09, the roads form): keep the stale flood reuse for speed (LOGISTICS.md § 4, written same day) and remove the parallel roads it leaves THIS SPRINT. MEASURED (road_stale_flood_probe, merged aa007264; 16 curated seeds pooled): STALE 79,154 road tiles vs FRESH 73,503; long parallel pairs d1 K8 235 vs 103 (history-history 176 vs 42); history route cost gap 1.87% vs 0.96%; pass time gen+hist 184+88 s vs 416+419 s loaded (seed 0 gen 15->77 s, hist 7->62 s). Half of history corridors change under FRESH; split nations 47 vs 54. Example: seed 37, two history corridors from (229,71) run side by side 17 tiles. CANDIDATES (measure, then pick the cheapest that meets the done-when): (1) targeted refresh - after a stamp, rebuild only the floods whose settled region the stamp could shorten (e.g. destinations within a cost radius of the stamped tiles), or re-route a pending corridor whose cached path runs within d of a newer road; (2) post-pass merge - detect parallel runs (the probe's d/K measure) and drop or merge the redundant run onto the existing road, connectivity held; (3) BL-1077's bounded per-village spur search priced on the field as it stands (spurs only). DONE WHEN: long parallel pairs (d1 K8) at or below FRESH's 103 pooled, road_generation_harness green (connectivity, R2s-b), pass time within ~1.25x of STALE, digests move once (re-bless at the sprint close).

items.author: Ben (2026-10-10, the sprint 53 nation-player session); filed by Claude
items.title: Hit the total and major nation targets every time, by a lean and then in-world reconciliation
items.design: DIRECTION RULED (Ben, 2026-10-10, option C; always hit): NATION_GENERATION.md § The nation count is a target. Total <= 40, major 1..6, total >= major. Stage 1, the lean: the total sets placement seed density; the major target leans charter-capital concentration. Stage 2, reconciliation by history verbs: conquest/absorption (too many nations), a subject freed or a province seceding (too few), a national champion chartered in the richest championless minor (too few majors), a cross-border buy-out (too many majors). OPEN before build: which span runs reconciliation; how the richest minor is read; buy-out pricing; how the merge pass's min-territory stop composes with a target. MEASURE FIRST: the natural total and major counts across the 16 library seeds (living polities run ~40-115, so the 40 cap reconciles on nearly every seed). Gate: every library seed lands on both targets across a grid of target pairs, each correction recorded as a history event.
